newsitem.title: USA: Neurogen extends programs with Pfizer.
newsitem.headline: Neurogen extends programs with Pfizer.

text.p: Neurogen Corp said Wednesday it planned a two-year, $10.4 million extension of its GABA receptor based research and development programs with Pfizer Inc, covering drugs to treat anxiety, sleep disorders, and cognition impairment.
The addition, the company announced revised clinical development plans in its anti-anxiety program.

The new agreement extends the research programs under the 1992 Neurogen/Pfizer collaboration covering drugs for anxiety and cognition enhancement and the 1994 alliance to develop drugs for sleep disorders and combines both programs. The 1992 program was scheduled to expire at the end of this year, and the 1994 sleep disorders program could have ended as early as June 1997.

The new agreement combines scientific resources committed under both agreements and extends both collaborations through December 1998. The dual extension will provide Neurogen $5.2 million per year in added funded research payments in 1997 and 1998, totaling $10.4 million over the two year extension period.

The goal of the Neurogen/Pfizer GABA receptor-based collaborative programs is to discover and develop a set of drug candidates addressing the existing therapeutic needs in each of the three target indications: anxiety, sleep disorders and cognition impairment.

As is common in small molecule drug discovery at pharmaceutical companies, early lead candidates may provide the initial evidence supporting the clinical validity of a given mechanism of action, while later candidates may be refined to possess superior pharmaceutical utility. Such a circumstance has led to the joint decision to transfer the development focus of the anxiolytic program to a newer drug candidate designated NGD 91-2.

The Neurogen/Pfizer anxiety program has demonstrated that a small molecule drug candidate acting on a specific set of GABA receptor subtypes can provide quick relief from anxiety without the sedation associated with currently marketed drugs such as Valium and Xanax. Due to the information and experience collected during the NGD 91-1 clinical program, Pfizer will be able to conduct the Phase I clinical trials on NGD 91-2 on an accelerated schedule.
